title: Audit findings — what this round checked and what it found

findings.finding: The site's injury join uses a five-club depth pilot while a 31-club depth collection already sits in the repository.
findings.evidence: The site reports 6 "listed starters ruled Out". The same join run across the 31 clubs already collected returns 30. No published value is wrong; the published number is a floor presented as if it were the population.
findings.source_label: example club depth chart (each row carries its own)
findings.fix: Published on pages/availability.html: the full join is the main table, the pilot is kept below it as a labelled subset, and the coverage is stated on the page. The remaining decision for the owner is whether that becomes the permanent presentation (Q-19).

findings.finding: The live-pipeline tree (15 pages) was not linked from the landing page and appeared in no navigation.
findings.evidence: tools/check_links.py asserted reachability for every page tree except live/, so 15 pages could only be reached by typing the URL. The nav list in tools/build_site.py had no entry for it either. Reproduced with `python3 tools/check_links.py` before the fix.
findings.fix: Add live/ to the landing page and the nav, and make check_links.py assert reachability for it.

findings.finding: The verify-site workflow was red on main: tools/check_links.py failed with 111 errors.
findings.evidence: Two causes. (a) It scanned raw HTML and treated JavaScript template strings such as href="${s.url}" as internal links. (b) It applied the main site's stylesheet contract to the live/ tree, which uses its own stylesheet and JS-rendered navigation. Neither was a defect in the published pages.
findings.fix: Strip JS template literals before link assertions, and give live/ its own contract check.

findings.finding: 301 of 345 injury rows had never been re-checked by a second reader (flag I-17).
findings.evidence: This round transcribed all 345 rows from the official page independently and diffed every cell: 2,183 cells across the four tables, 0 mismatches. I-17 can be closed.
findings.fix: Done — tools/verify_against_official.py now runs this diff on every build.

findings.finding: The landing page's flag count is hardcoded in prose and can drift from data/flags.json.
findings.evidence: The hero button and the "13 open flags" wording are generated from a computed length, but a human reading of the count elsewhere (README, coordination log) already disagrees: the research session counted 34 flagged items, the live session 6, the lab session 12, the dashboard 17. Four registers, four counts, no single queue.
findings.fix: One consolidated review queue generated from all registers (pages/review-queue.html).

findings.finding: The landing page said the dashboard publishes "no prices, correlations or strategy results", but four other trees in the same repository publish exactly those.
findings.evidence: research/, dashboard/lab-*, site/ and live/ all publish computed lines, correlations or strategy results. The sentence was true of pages/ only. A reader arriving at the landing page would reasonably conclude the repository contains none.
findings.source_label: the benchmark the computed values rest on
findings.fix: Reworded to distinguish league-published tables from computed values, and link every tree.

findings.finding: The invented-line and strategy pages present computed numbers without labelling which of them are NOT league-published.
findings.evidence: data/lines/*.csv and data/strategies/* hold computed values derived from a third-party benchmark. The research tree states this on every page; the pages/ tree does not carry the same label, so the same number appears with two different levels of caveat.
findings.source_label: the league publishes no betting prices
findings.fix: Owner decision pending on the badge (suggestions board B-07). Not implemented unilaterally because it changes how published numbers are labelled across four trees.

findings.finding: The official standings table prints LA for the Rams; the repository's standings.tsv prints LAR; the injury report prints LAR.
findings.evidence: Both are the same club and both spellings are printed by an official page, so no value is wrong. It is recorded because a join on the team code silently drops the Rams if the alias is not applied.
findings.fix: Alias handled in tools/verify_against_official.py; no data change made.

findings.finding: The standings table prints LAST 5 for all 32 clubs; the published file carries the column header but no values.
findings.evidence: Available-but-unpublished, not wrong. Reported by tools/verify_against_official.py under available_but_unpublished_columns rather than as a mismatch, so it stays visible without overstating it as an error.
findings.fix: Either publish the column or drop the header; owner's choice, listed on the suggestions board.

findings.finding: The four trees use different line benchmarks, so their ROIs are not comparable with each other.
findings.evidence: The research lab names a third-party closing line carried in nflverse/nfldata; the analytics lab marks every strategy NOT ELIGIBLE for undocumented provenance; the annex uses nfldata lines; the live tree publishes no prices at all.
findings.source_label: the mirror that carries the attributed line
findings.fix: Owner decision Q-02 picks one reference; until then results stay labelled per tree.
